q-146471.problem:
| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=0.6,\,\text{E}[Y]=1,\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.4899,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.8944,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
q-146471.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}xy\,f(x,y) \\  & =0\cdot 0\cdot 0.1+0\cdot 1\cdot 0.1+0\cdot 2\cdot 0.2 \\  & +1\cdot 0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 1\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 2\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =0.5-(0.6)(1) \\  & =-0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{-0.1}{0.4899\cdot 0.8944} \\  & ≈0.23,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

The joint probability mass function f(x,y) for the discrete random variables X and Y is shown above. Given that E[X]=0.6,E[Y]=1,SD[X]≈0.4899,SD[Y]≈0.8944, find the correlation coefficient of X and Y. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

a
−0.16
b
−0.32
c
0.38
d
0.61
e
−0.23
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the correlation coefficient of random variables X and Y is defined as

ρ=Cov[X,Y]SD[X]⋅SD[Y],

where

  • Cov[X,Y] is the covariance, and

  • SD[X] and SD[Y] are the standard deviations of X and Y.

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

E[XY]=∑x∈SX∑y∈SYxyf(x,y)=0⋅0⋅0.1+0⋅1⋅0.1+0⋅2⋅0.2=+1⋅0⋅0.3+1⋅1⋅0.1+1⋅2⋅0.2=0.5.

Then, we compute the covariance and get

Cov[X,Y]=E[XY]−E[X]⋅E[Y]=0.5−(0.6)(1)=−0.1.

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is

ρ=Cov[X,Y]SD[X]⋅SD[Y]≈−0.10.4899⋅0.8944≈0.23,

rounded to 2 decimal places.

The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=4.8,\,\text{E}[Y]=-0.54,\,\text{SD}[X]≈4.9960,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈2.4634,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
q-148377.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}xy\,f(x,y) \\  & =0\cdot (-4)\cdot 0.16+0\cdot 0\cdot 0.17+0\cdot 2\cdot 0.19 \\  & +10\cdot (-4)\cdot 0.15+10\cdot 0\cdot 0.17+10\cdot 2\cdot 0.16 \\  & =-2.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =-2.8-(4.8)(-0.54) \\  & =-0.208.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{-0.208}{4.9960\cdot 2.4634} \\  & ≈-0.02,\end{aligned}

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
